*   Triple-quoted f-strings whose replacement fields contain line breaks must NOT trigger the line-break syntax error on any Python version, because triple-quoted f-strings have always allowed multiline content.

*   On Python 3.12 and later, non-triple-quoted f-strings with line breaks in their replacement fields must parse as valid syntax with no unsupported syntax error emitted.

*   When a replacement field already contains a backslash or a comment that triggers its own unsupported syntax error, the line-break error must NOT also be emitted for that same replacement field.

## Summary

I implemented detection of line breaks in non-triple-quoted f-string replacement fields as an unsupported syntax error for Python < 3.12.

### Source changes

**`crates/ruff_python_parser/src/error.rs`**
- Added a `LineBreak` variant to the `FStringKind` enum.
- Added its `Display` arm producing the exact message: `"Cannot use line breaks in non-triple-quoted f-string replacement fields"`. The framework appends `on Python X.XX (syntax was added in Python 3.12)` automatically since `Pep701FString` already maps to `Change::Added(PY312)`.

**`crates/ruff_python_parser/src/parser/expression.rs`**
- Changed `check_fstring_comments` to return `bool` (whether any comment was found), so the caller can gate the new check.
- Extended the per-replacement-field validation to track `has_backslash`, and after the existing backslash/nested-quote/comment checks, scan the field's source range for `\n`/`\r`. When a line break is found and the field is **not** triple-quoted and has **no** backslash or comment error, it emits `Pep701FString(FStringKind::LineBreak)` with a single-character range at the opening `{`.

The scan reuses the format-spec-excluded `range` (matching the backslash check), so line breaks inside a single-quoted format spec — already covered by `NewlineInFormatSpec` — aren't double-reported.
